title: Morning Cybersecurity Digest
subtitle: Monday, October 12 — Here's what's worth your attention today.

items.title: CVSS 10.0 flaw in argocd-mcp exposes AI coding agent pipelines
items.summary: Apiiro researchers disclosed CVE-2026-82456 in argocd-mcp 0.8.0, an MCP server that links AI coding agents to Argo CD. Unauthenticated attackers could abuse stored Argo CD tokens in exposed HTTP deployments to create and deploy applications from attacker-controlled repositories.
items.details: Apiiro's broader scan found 375 of 525 MCP packages using HTTP or SSE transports without Origin validation. Fix: upgrade to argocd-mcp 0.9.0+, rotate tokens, review application and sync activity.
items.action: If you run argocd-mcp, upgrade to 0.9.0 or later immediately, rotate all Argo CD tokens, and audit recent deploy/sync activity for rogue apps.

items.title: CISA slaps five N-day flaws on KEV with rare 3-day federal deadline
items.summary: CISA added five old but actively exploited flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct 8: CVE-2015-3306 (ProFTPD, 10.0), CVE-2021-3199 (ONLYOFFICE, 9.8), CVE-2023-22894 (Strapi, 7.2), CVE-2016-3081 (Apache Struts, 8.1) and CVE-2015-5477 (ISC BIND, 7.5).
items.details: Federal agencies were given a three-day patch-or-decommission window (deadline Oct 11). A joint advisory from seven nations attributes the campaign to Chinese state-linked actors associated with Integrity Technology Group.
items.action: Treat any exposed ProFTPD, ONLYOFFICE Docs, Strapi, Apache Struts or BIND instance as compromised: patch now and run forensic triage, not just updates.

items.title: Super Forms WordPress plugin lets strangers delete your whole site
items.summary: CVE-2026-17609 (CVSS 9.1) is an unauthenticated arbitrary directory deletion flaw in Super Forms Drag & Drop Form Builder 6.3.316 and earlier. Any visitor who can reach a form can delete the site's files and uploads when an affected setting is enabled.
items.details: Fixed in 6.3.317 (and 6.4.008 on the beta line). The same release also patched an unauthenticated file read (CVE-2026-28167) and an upload extension bypass (CVE-2026-17196).
items.action: Update past 6.3.317 at once, verify you have off-site backups, and check for unexpected deletions or injected files on any public WordPress host.

items.title: Emperador claims Spelman Logistics, demands $500K
items.summary: The Emperador ransomware group listed US transport firm Spelman Logistics on its leak site on Oct 11, claiming theft from the company's MVMNT transportation management system plus unnamed partners' systems.
items.details: Claimed haul: 1.2M contact records, 245K carrier profiles with tax and Social Security data, 57K bank account records with routing numbers, and 4.5M carrier registry entries. $500,000 ransom demanded in Bitcoin or Monero. No screenshots posted; figures are the gang's unverified claims.

items.title: Incransom lists Manitoba's flagship hospital, HSC Winnipeg
items.summary: ThreatMon spotted Incransom adding hsc.mb.ca — Health Sciences Centre Winnipeg, Manitoba's major trauma, neurosurgery, burn, transplant and psychiatric hospital — to its victim list on Oct 11.
items.details: A leak-site listing is not proof of intrusion, data theft or service disruption; the hospital has not confirmed the claim. Healthcare stays a prime target for its data sensitivity and downtime pressure.

items.title: Majinahanashi claims Spanish logistics major Grupo Caliche
items.summary: Majinahanashi listed Grupo Caliche — a Spanish international logistics, freight and telecom company — on its leak site, discovered Oct 10, with the initial attack estimated as early as Aug 11, 2026.
items.details: No attack vector, encryption status or exfiltration volume disclosed; the claim is unverified. Notably, Majinahanashi also just listed an India-based target (see India section).

items.title: Hyderabad police bust ₹60–70 crore mule-account network, arrest two
items.summary: Hyderabad Cybercrime Police arrested Gumma Ramesh (39) and Mudale Anil (19) of Ramanthapur for allegedly collecting ~70 mule bank accounts and SIM cards and supplying them to cybercriminals for commissions.
items.details: Police say the accounts touch ~450 cybercrime cases across India worth ₹60–70 crore. The probe began from a Facebook old-currency-note scam where a victim lost ₹7,93,351. Case booked under IT Act 66C/66D and BNS provisions.

items.title: Eclipse ransomware lists Indian manufacturer simplexengg.in
items.summary: The Eclipse ransomware group added simplexengg.in, an Indian manufacturing firm, to its leak site on Oct 8. Eclipse runs a double-extortion model — exfiltrating data before encryption.
items.details: Manufacturing is a favorite target: production downtime converts directly into ransom pressure. The listing is the group's claim and is unverified.

items.title: Majinahanashi names India's BONJOUR GROUP on its leak site
items.summary: The Majinahanashi ransomware group listed BONJOUR GROUP, an India-based organization, on Oct 10. The group has ~42 recorded victims and follows the standard double-extortion playbook.
items.details: No victim sector details or claimed data volumes published yet; treat as an unverified threat-actor claim until corroborated.
